text: FBI probes suspected hack of US crime database. The Federal Bureau of Investigation is “investigating a suspected cyberattack on its National Crime Information Centre (NCIC), a nationwide database used by law enforcement agencies across the United States to share criminal justice information.” The suspected intrusion was discovered in recent days, with two people briefed on the investigation telling CNN that hackers apparently gained access to the system. The development, reported by CNN on Friday, marks the second reported cyber intrusion involving FBI systems in recent months. KCRA3 on Saturday reported that a former FBI cybercrime investigations official (name withheld) warned CNN that the concern was not “merely whether hackers accessed sensitive information, but whether they could compromise the accuracy of records used by police officers. The NCIC serves as a central information-sharing platform for federal, state and local law enforcement agencies, providing access to records on outstanding warrants, wanted individuals, criminal histories and information used for background checks. A former FBI official who previously led investigations into cybercriminal groups told CNN that the database was critical to day-to-day policing, as officers across the country rely on it to identify wanted fugitives and check outstanding warrants. The former official also raised concerns about the possibility of hackers compromising the accuracy of information contained in the database, warning that incorrect records could affect decisions made by law enforcement officers. The FBI did not immediately respond to requests for comment from CNN and Reuters. The suspected breach comes amid growing concerns over cybersecurity vulnerabilities affecting US government institutions and critical infrastructure, following a series of technological disruptions involving banks, the National Security Agency and the Federal Aviation Administration’s air traffic control systems. On Thursday, after FBI officials had reportedly learnt of the suspected intrusion, FBI Director Kash Patel appeared on Fox News to discuss the bureau’s cybersecurity efforts. Patel promoted Operation Winter Shield, an initiative aimed at encouraging organisations to strengthen their digital security and protect critical infrastructure. “Other administrations could have made these updates, but they didn’t,” he said, “We are staying ahead of the curve and making up for lost time.” In a separate post on X on Friday, Patel said the FBI was taking the fight against cybercriminals around the world under President Donald Trump’s leadership. “Through Operation Winter Shield, we’re going on offense against cyber threats, strengthening our nation’s defences, and working with our partners to protect American businesses, government systems, and critical infrastructure,” he wrote. The latest suspected intrusion follows a September breach of an FBI recruitment website by the digital extortion group ShinyHunters, which reportedly exposed personal information belonging to current and former bureau employees. The group claimed responsibility for that attack, which prompted an FBI investigation. However, the “identity of those responsible for the latest suspected intrusion, the method used to access the NCIC and whether any information was stolen or altered remain unclear.”
